cells.tense: You are reading the pattern here and now, with the pen still in your hand.
cells.act: feel it alongside them and keep your own side
cells.ask: When someone brings you something hard, keep your own read of it yours while you stay beside them in it. A few minutes is enough. No fixing, no reframing, no telling them what it means — let being there be the whole of it.
cells.core:
You can see what is true across the layers of a situation and not close the book on it. The pattern shows itself, and you let it keep showing you more. That is knowing that deepens instead of hardening into a verdict, and the ones near you tend to feel steadier for it. The floor holds because you are standing on it.

The growing edge is the other side of that: being with someone's hard thing without vanishing into their version of it. So when a person tells you something difficult, stay beside them in it — not to fix it, not to hand it back reframed. Keep what you see as yours. They get someone who is not carrying it alone; you get to still be somebody while you do it. Both of those matter, and this is where they happen.
cells.sheetLine: You see the whole thing and still let it keep showing you more.
cells.verb: seeing the whole pattern of a thing, including its layers
cells.place: where endurance is held and weight is carried without breaking

cells.tense: You are bracing at a version of the situation that has not arrived yet, and reading it as already written.
cells.act: choose this, not that, and mean it
cells.ask: Pick one step that is actually here now, and mean it — this, not the other thing your verdict predicts. No defending the whole call, no winning with it. Just the step you choose.
cells.core:
When this runs hot, you see how it all fits together so clearly that the reading turns into a verdict. You know how it ends, you know what someone is, and nothing new is getting in. From outside it looks like certainty; from where you stand it feels like solid ground. But solid ground is not the whole room, and nothing shifts while the ending is already decided.

What is asked is not less sight — it is direction. Pick one step that is genuinely here, and mean it. This, not the thing you predicted. Leave the verdict where it is; you do not need to argue it down. Choosing from what is present gets you off the future you were braced against, and the pattern gets to be wrong about something.
cells.sheetLine: You are so sure how this ends that it cannot change.

cells.tense: You read the pattern clearly once, and you are still standing at a door that is already behind you.
cells.act: open the thing you have been assuming you knew and look at it unlabelled
cells.ask: Look at something in your life without the name you have been giving it. A person, a situation, a habit — meet it as if you had just come across it. No label, no story about what it is, and let what you notice stand.
cells.core:
The eye for what is true across the layers is still yours. It has gone quiet. You keep asking what it all means, and the asking circles without touching down, while the living version of the thing sits there unexamined. Sight needs material to work on. That comes from looking, and looking has gone still.

So meet something without the label on it — not naive, this is how seeing comes back. If the pull arrives to work out what it means, let that wait; a fresh look is not a conclusion and does not have to become one. What you find may be exactly what you already had. What changes is that this time you were there for it.
cells.sheetLine: You can still see it — you just stopped looking at it.

cells.tense: You are already reading what is true here, and you have been giving the credit to something else.
cells.act: let an exchange flow both ways
cells.ask: Take what someone hands you — help, time, a straight answer — without immediately working out how to square it. Let one exchange finish with you having received, no tally on the other end, and no plan to even it up later.
cells.core:
You are reading what is true across the layers of a situation. When asked how you knew, you point at luck, or at them, or at how plain it all was. Your name has not been going on it. It arrives for you before it arrives for most, and over time that has gotten filed as nothing special — just how the ordinary thing looks.

So keep the exchange honest instead of counting your side. Give what you give, and let something come back without checking whether it should. Where you have been waving off what arrives, let one thing land and stay put. That two-way flow is the older form of this line, the one that ran before anything needed attributing. Receiving is not the same as owing.
cells.sheetLine: What you notice is yours, and you keep leaving the credit elsewhere.

attempts.check: The record gives me the four statuses of one capacity but never the person's history, so the most I can say about where a reading lands is which face is showing now — I cannot know whether someone has been holding a long strain, who leaned on them, or how a pattern got decided; every Too Little cell stays on where the person stands, not why. A reader could fairly say the Too Much cell reads condemnation as cruelty when the record's own face is finality — recognition wearing down into a verdict — so the core names the closing, not the meanness, and the ask is only about choosing one thing again, which survives being wrong about the diagnosis. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is any line about a person who has been seen too fully or judged too long — cut before the cells. The asks come from the partners' own acts and hold even if the status is wrong: choosing direction, looking again at what you already know, letting an exchange move both ways, and letting another person's answer be the point are all useful regardless of which face is showing.
